answers.1_quality_preserved: Mostly. Full 1000-example verifier pass 0.843 vs corrected BF16 0.864 (−2.1 pp) and bnb INT8 0.866. Invalid parse 0.0. Material drop on execution_vs_imagery 1.000 → 0.784 (−21.6 pp); other seven families flat or slightly improved.
answers.2_vram_40pct: Yes on weights: model VRAM 4.27 GiB vs HF BF16 7.94 GB (−46.2%) and vs vLLM BF16 load 7.78 GB (−45.1%). Peak using EngineCore weights+activation 5.39 GB vs HF peak 8.16 GB (−34.1%). Serving nvidia-smi is dominated by KV-cache reservation at gpu_memory_utilization and is not the comparison metric.
answers.3_faster_than_bnb: Yes. Decode 134.3 tok/s vs bnb INT8 12.5 (+974%) and H.4 fair bnb 18.73 (+617%). E2E 476.5 ms vs 5450 ms.
answers.4_vs_vllm_bf16: Faster on this single-request contract: 134.3 vs 61.3 tok/s (+119%), E2E 476.5 vs 1043.8 ms. vLLM BF16 still had runtime LoRA; W8A8 is a merged checkpoint. TTFT not exposed in offline LLM.generate for either.
answers.5_production_int8_candidate: Yes — this is the production INT8 candidate (compressed-tensors W8A8 + vLLM Cutlass INT8). bitsandbytes INT8 remains rejected. Quality caveat on execution_vs_imagery must be reviewed before locking as the only production path.
answers.6_remaining_bottleneck: Quality: execution_vs_imagery sensitivity to W8A8. Systems: KV-cache still dominates serving VRAM at high gpu_memory_utilization; INT8 linear is no longer the slow path (Cutlass INT8 decode exceeds vLLM BF16 on this bench).
answers.7_further_kernel_work: NO. Native CutlassInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel is selected and already beats both bnb INT8 and vLLM BF16 decode on the locked single-request contract. Custom Triton/CUDA kernel work is not justified by these measurements.
